mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) relative to its 3-month moving average compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days. This mechanism operates continuously without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: The mechanism fails if 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines over the prior 3 months (rolling 3-month change < 0).

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 4.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering risk-off sentiment and negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days due to reduced consumer spending expectations.
failure_condition: The mechanism fails if 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 4.0.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1250 and retail sales (RSAFS) below 500000 indicates weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days through reduced corporate earnings forecasts.
failure_condition: The mechanism fails if 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when both HOUST < 1250 and RSAFS < 500000.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle characterized by FEDFUNDS > 2.5 and CPIAUCSL > 250 (index level), rising interest rates and inflationary pressure reduce equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The mechanism fails if 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 2.5 and CPIAUCSL > 250.

mechanism_narrative: Positive quarterly growth in real GDP (GDPC1) signals expanding economic activity, supporting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days. This is an always-on trend signal.
failure_condition: The mechanism fails if 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 growth rate (quarterly) is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0 indicates manufacturing contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days due to reduced corporate output and profit margins.
failure_condition: The mechanism fails if 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100.0.

mechanism_narrative: Labor market slack (UNRATE > 4.0 and PAYEMS growth rate < 0.5% monthly) fuels recession concerns, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days through reduced consumer spending and equity risk aversion.
failure_condition: The mechanism fails if 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 4.0 and PAYEMS_growth < 0.5.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in FEDFUNDS above 2.5 and CPIAUCSL above 250 (index level) signals inflationary monetary tightening, reducing liquidity and equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The mechanism fails if 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 2.5 and CPIAUCSL > 250.
